// Expected values for the butcher's work (docs/rules/butchering.md), captured from the original program in the emulator (ADR 0008):
// tools/GhidraDump/emulate.py, the verb goods with a finished butcher's shop (type 13, a large building) at a flag, reduced to the passes that
// matter. The building's flag pointer (+0xe, which its handler 0x42e1b3 keeps its pig request through) is set by hand, as a built site
// leaves it (0x43ef82). The castle's start stock is that of the level 30: it holds the butcher's knife (good 19), so the castle makes its
// jobless settler (slot 3) the butcher, as the request's second way does (0x42be63). A scenario starts with a "#" line that names its verb
// command; each line after it gives, for a pass, the 16 bytes of the butcher (s3=) where his node, state, or part of the work changed, the
// 18 bytes of the building (b=, its flag pointer left out) where they changed, the flag's byte 4 and goods bytes (g=) where they changed, the
// request words of the flag (req=, the bytes 0x42 to 0x45) where they changed, the castle's pig count (pig=) and meat count (meat=) where
// they changed, and the generator's words (rng=) as they stand. The puts of the command lay the pigs (good 2) or stones (good 10) on the
// places of a flag by hand. The flags are listed in the order the engine numbers them (by column). The scenario flag-full ends at the pass 1241,
// the first place the carriers free: the butcher waits at the door with the meat from the pass 1173 while eight stones lie on the flag from
// the pass 1000. After it the engine's carriers leave the flag's node earlier than the original's, so the next place frees at another pass
// (the open lead of the carriers' hand-over that docs/rules/milling.md names, not the butcher's). Not production code: no routine of the program is transcribed here, only values the program produced.
